comments.text: caber toss's entry, from the shell: practice or not ($08 from $081D), the number of players ($09 from $081E), no player yet ($0A = 0), the first attempt ($0B = 1), the music's frequency table ($244A); then the set-up ($103D)
the shell's unpacker reads the packed file's header here ($1000-$1004) while it unpacks; once unpacked, caber toss's CLD
the packed file's header, its third byte, read by the shell's unpacker; here, the LDA of LDA $081D
the header's fourth byte, read by the shell's unpacker; here, the operand's low byte
the header's last byte, read by the shell's unpacker; here, the operand's high byte
each new attempt, from "TRY AGAIN?" or the fire button ($15A4): the screen off, the sprite shapes' swap reset, and if the second set was swapped in ($74), all 18 pages swapped back ($1EB2)

the set-up: the swap's addresses reset, the stack, the hardware's interrupt vector at $FFFE pointed at $1268, RAM everywhere but the I/O, zero page $20-$FF cleared; the field's rows of grass, the text rows, and the top six rows from $8000 into both screens with their colours from $8800; multicolour, VIC bank 1, the raster interrupt at line 0 through $0314 ($1407) starting at $141E; the thrower at x $0190, y $78, the caber at x $01CC, y $75, the caber upright ($6D = 2), the scenery drawn ($197A, $19DB); the thrower lifting the caber ($5E = 1); the player's name and the attempt in the text rows; the music silenced and tune 1; the screen on, and the idle loop

the screen: rows 15 to 22 and 24 of both screens filled with character 2, rows 6 and 23 with character $F7, row 24's colour white and rows 6 and 23 green; rows 0 to 5 from $8000 into both screens, their colours from $8800
row 4 of the top rows into the second screen
the video chip, the interrupts, and the thrower's and caber's places
a competition: the next player ($0A); after the last, the next attempt ($0B), and after the third back to the shell ($0900)
the player's name, 16 characters from their record, the digits 1 to 9 through the table at $12B7, into row 24 of both screens
a letter: its screen code plus $D1
the frame counter at $0900, tune 1, the screen on
the main loop does nothing: everything happens in the interrupts
the interrupt, through $FFFE since the KERNAL is switched out: A, X and Y saved, then on through $0314, or $0316 for a BRK, as the KERNAL would
where each attempt's text is: "FIRST TOSS ", "SECOND TOSS", "THIRD TOSS "
each attempt's colour: cyan, yellow, orange
the text "TRY AGAIN" with its question mark, stored as "!"
the characters for the digits 0 to 9 in the event's character set
the answers' characters, N and Y
draws the caber: unless its pose ($3C) is negative, the pose's sprites from $9000 at the caber's place ($6A-$6B plus the view's offset $58, y $42), from sprite 4 on
draws the thrower: sprites off, the pose ($2A) from $9000 at the thrower's place ($50-$51 plus $58, y $52), from sprite 0; with $5F set only the count's low two bits of sprites; then on through $1330

each sprite of the pose: its x and ninth bit, y, pointer ((address - $4000) / 64) into both screens, and from the shape's 64th byte its colour, multicolour, double width and double height; on to the end of the pose ($13E0)
the shape's 64th byte, the address written by $135D and $1365
the operand of CPX #: the end of the pose's sprites
each sprite's bit, twice over, by twice the sprite's number
each sprite's bit cleared, twice over
the raster interrupt: acknowledged, then on through the JMP at $1415 to the handler for this line ($141E, $14F1, $1532)
JMP $FFFF: the next handler's address written into $1416-$1417
the interrupt's end: Y, X and A back, and RTI

at line $FA: the next handler at line $60 ($14F1); the top band's settings: multicolour with the fine scroll at 4, the screen in use and the characters at $7800, light blue background and light grey and grey multicolours; the frame counter ($2F-$30) counts up; then, unless the last frame's work still runs ($7B), interrupts on and the frame's work: the thrower's pose list ($1DC3), the caber's own moves ($1EE7), both drawn ($12F6, $12C3), the end of the attempt ($156A), the caber's balance ($2350), the joystick and the run ($15E5), the sprite shapes' swap ($1EB2), the end of a good toss, and the music ($2493)
with nothing else going on, the lean's count ($6E-$6F) eased back $60 a frame; when it passes 0, the balance once more
one more page of the second set of shapes swapped in, while no scroll was drawn this frame ($7F)
when the frame counter reaches exactly $0200 and $7A is 0 (64 frames after a good toss): tune 2, the thrower walks off ($5E = 5), the attempt over ($20 = 5), the thrower at x $18 and y $C0
the music, unless a scroll was drawn this frame
at line $60: the next handler at line $E8 ($1532); the field's fine scroll ($21); green and dark grey and light grey multicolours
at line $EA: black for the text rows, then from line $EE single colour with the fine scroll at 4; while the run goes on ($67) the stamina runs down ($1A32); the next handler at line $FA ($141E)

the attempt's end, once the attempt is over ($20 = 5) and the thrower is not dropping, falling or walking off (states 4, 6, 7): in practice "TRY AGAIN?" with Y or N, up and down choosing; the fire button pressed and let go: the screen off and either the next attempt ($101A) or, with N in practice, back to the shell
the fire button: pressed, then let go
let go: the next attempt, or back to the shell
Y, the answer to start with

the joystick: $80 is the player's port, port 2 until it is known; on the first attempt the first port with anything pressed, after 7 frames, is kept for the player ($195C); the fire button reads as up ($81 clear) until the caber is lifted. Then, while the attempt runs ($20 = 0), the run ($16A9), and the fire button: with the caber leaning forward too far ($6D 3 or more) the caber is dropped ($23ED); otherwise the toss begins (state 3)
no fire button until the caber is lifted
the caber's own moves over ($63 = $FF), the music silenced: with stamina left, the attempt over ($20 = 5), the thrower's state 4, tune 4, the frame counter at $0340, where it never ends the attempt
the caber's own moves not over
with no stamina left: the thrower's state 4, the frame counter at $0340, the stamina 3, tune 3; the caber $42 pixels right of $72-$73, its pose, moves and step by the lean ($1911, $1916, $191B)

the run: speed ($31-$32) over 4 into $5A-$5B. Fire not pressed: $1707. Fire pressed and the toss not begun: the caber taken back ($1A6B); leaning 3 or more the caber is dropped ($23ED), otherwise the toss begins: state 3, the caber's pose from $190C, the speed kept ($60-$61)
fire up: once the toss has begun ($2E positive) the release ($1AD0): the caber thrown ($2E = $FF), on to $18A5; after that its flight ($1B53) and its landing ($22AC)
the stride: the speed's band ($24, 0 to 15); while moving, every 16 frames, the stick's left or right, against the pose, steps the scroll a column ($1920)

the field's fine scroll ($21); the stride's counter ($25) gains the band's step ($18FC); on its overflow the stride's state ($29) moves on by the stick: left ($18E4), right ($18DC), or neither ($18D4)
a stride state that pushes ($18EC) adds speed: $1904 by the band, less the caber's lean (from $37-$38), never below 0
friction: the speed loses $18F4 by the band, not below 0
the speed's low byte, before the friction comes off it
with speed at least $30, the view's place ($33-$35) gains it, and the fine scroll follows
a new column while the toss runs: the thrower's place moves ($58), or the speed stops at the pose limits
the thrower's x offset less one
the view's column ($28) from its place; a new one redraws the scenery ($19DB), a step at a time ($23)
the next step of the redraw
the stride's next state with no stick, by the state
the next state with right held
the next state with left held
whether each stride state pushes, 1, and its counter
the friction by the speed's band
the stride counter's step by the band
the push's speed by the band
the caber's pose for the toss, by the lean
the caber's pose after it stood, by the lean
the thrower's next pose ($2A): from $16 to $1B over and over, setting $67 at the wrap; poses $19 and $16 start tunes 5 and 6, once each
the player's port: on the first attempt kept in $1971 for the player, after that read back from it
RTS, and the first byte of the ports kept
the ports kept for players 2 to 8

the scenery's 11 rows, from the map at $8170 at the view's column plus one, 128 bytes to a map row, into rows 7 to 17 of the screen not shown ($22: $4400 while $4000 is shown, and the other way round)
the copy, a row at a time
LDA $FFFF,Y and STA $FFFF,Y, their addresses written by $197A
the map row's address, low byte
the map row's address, high byte
the screen row's address, low byte
the screen row's address, high byte
swaps the screens ($22, $D018) and copies the 11 rows' colours from $8970 at the view's column into rows 7 to 17 of colour RAM
the colour map's address, high byte

the thrower's stamina ($37-$38, $0180 at the start), while the attempt runs: it loses one every four frames ($4D); once below $B0 it drops to 0 and the caber's own moves list 2 begins. A stamina of 3, set when the caber was stood up again, stays as it is
the stamina left as it is

fire held before the release: a balance step ($6D) of 3 becomes 4; once the toss has begun, the caber's height follows the thrower's pose ($2159) and the hold's count ($39-$3A) grows by the run's speed's high byte plus one each frame; each time the count passes the next threshold ($1CC2) the caber tilts a step further ($36), and at 5 it falls ($63 = 1); its pose by the tilt from $1CBC
the hold's count ($39) against the threshold for the next lean
the operand of CMP #, the lean's next threshold, written from $1CC2

the release: tune 7, the thrower's throw ($5E = 2); the caber's speed across ($43-$45) a quarter of the run's speed kept ($60-$61) plus the stamina less $1CC8 by the hold's count; its speed up ($46-$48) at $1B19; its spin's time ($49) from $1D04
the speed up: half the stamina, plus $1CC8 at the index $2C, less $30
the spin's time, from $1D04 by the stamina
the caber in the air: while the thrower's poses run, the caber rides with them ($2163); after them it moves by its speeds ($1B92)
the caber's height by the thrower's pose
the caber riding with the thrower

the caber's place gains its speeds; at the landing height ($1BBF) it lands: its pose from $2321, $64 set, the landing's place ($1C2B), tune 3, its spin's time halved; otherwise its speed up loses $0A10 a frame and its speed across $50, not below 0, and the spin ($1C0D)
the operand of CMP #: the height at which the caber lands, $A8 while it is held and then the spin's pose's value from $1CB3
the spin: when its time ($49) runs out, the caber's next pose of eight ($36), the landing height for that pose ($1CB3) into the CMP at $1BBE, and the time again
the caber's place on landing, moved by its pose ($1C91 across, $1CA2 down)
the caber's place when it is let go, moved by its pose the other way ($1C91, $1CA2)

the caber's place for each of its poses: across ($1C91), down ($1CA2), its spin's poses ($1CB3), its poses by the lean ($1CBC), the lean's thresholds ($1CC2), the speeds up ($1CC8), the spin's times ($1D04)
the caber's height by its pose
the height at which the caber lands, by its pose in the spin, 0 to 7
the caber's pose by the tilt in the hold
the hold's thresholds, one for each tilt

a falling curve, $F8 down to 0 at $1D04: the speed across takes the entry at the hold's count ($3A) from the stamina's low byte; the speed up adds the entry at 255 less three quarters of the count. But $3A only counts $39 passing 255, and $39 grows from 0 at each attempt ($103D) by the run speed's high byte plus 1 a frame, while a lean of 5, reached at $D4, fells the caber: $3A is 0 at the release, the speed across always takes $F8, and the speed up reads index 255, $1DC7, past the table and into the code: $C6, the opcode of DEC $5D
a rising curve, 0 up to $FF over 191 entries: the spin's times, by twice the stamina's high bits ($4A)

the thrower's pose list by the state ($5E): 1 lifting ($2060), 2 the throw ($2072), 3 the toss begun ($207E), 4 ($20B0), 5 ($20D6), 6 dropping the caber ($2132), 7 falling ($2092); each step a pose ($2A) and its frames ($5D); $FF ends the state ($5E = 0). In the fall and the drop, poses $5B and $4E end the attempt with a fault ($4C) and $65 and $56 give the result ($2170) with tune 4; $5F tunes 3
state 1: at its end the caber is held ($3C = $12) a little left
the step: $FF frames ends the state
the pose and its frames, and $5F by the state ($2151)
swaps one page of sprite shapes between $A000 on and $6640 on, 18 pages in all (192 bytes of the last), the second set of shapes for the toss
LDA $A000,Y / LDA $6640,Y, swapped, the pages stepped on afterwards
the high byte of LDA $A000,Y, the page of the second set, $A0 on; at $B2 the swap is over
the high byte of LDA $6640,Y, the page of the set in use
the high byte of STA $A000,Y, as $1EC9
the high byte of STA $6640,Y, as $1ECD

the caber's own moves ($63, 1 to 6) from the lists at $1F6A: each step 4 bytes, the pose ($FE keeps it), a move across and down, and its frames ($75); $FF ends them ($63 = $FF). In list 5 tune 8 now and then
the caber's own moves done for this frame
where each of the caber's own move lists is
the caber's move lists' high bytes
the lists: pose, across, down, frames, to $FF
the thrower's pose lists, poses and frames by state: 1 lifting: poses $38 to $3A, then $18 frames
state 5: $76, then $66 to $73 three times, $74 to $76
the caber's height by the thrower's pose from $1E
the caber's height by the thrower's pose from $30

the result in the text row: "FAULT" after a fault ($4C), or the distance between sprites 7 and 3 in feet (a foot for every 8 pixels, plus 10) and inches (from $2297 by the pixels left over and a bit read from colour RAM's unconnected upper half), kept in the player's record when it is the best ($2248)
X counted up in decimal into A
the player's best throw: feet ($0817) then inches ($0816); a better one replaces it, its text (feet, ', inches, ") into $0810-$0815
the same feet: by the inches
the inches by twice the pixels left over plus a random bit: 0 to 11

the caber landed ($64), the attempt still running: pose $0C ends it, as a fall short of x $0148 ($5E = 4), and shows the result; pose $10 is a good toss, the counter set to reach $0200 in 64 frames; other poses tip on, a pose every $49 frames, back ($4C = $80, a fault) or forward
the landing dealt with for this frame
RTS; also read as the first byte, $60, of the table at $2317 by $22DC
the caber's poses tipping forward, from $2319 by the lean
the caber's pose on landing, by its pose in the air
the caber fallen back ($7A): once the frame counter reaches $02xx, 8 frames on, the thrower falls (state 7), the caber's moves list 6, $7A = 5 so that it happens once, the thrower at x $18 and y $C0

the caber's balance while running: the change in speed since the last frame, over 16, adds to the lean's count ($6E); at 10 or more the caber tips forward a step ($6D), below -8 back a step, and the count starts again; at step 5 it is dropped ($23ED), below step 0 it falls back ($7A = 1, the frame counter $01F8, the run stopped at $2409); otherwise its pose ($23E8) and place ($23E3) by the step
the caber's pose and place by the step
the speed kept for the next frame
the caber's x offset from the thrower by the lean step
the caber's pose by the lean step
the caber dropped forward: the frame counter $0280, the thrower's drop ($5E = 6), the caber's moves list 5, the lean held at step 4; the run stopped ($2409), and back into the balance's step
the run stopped: $2E and $5F = $80, $67 = 0, the speed kept ($60-$61)

starts tune A: for each voice, the track the tune gives it ($28B5), its data pointer ($A0-$A5) and a wait of one frame ($C1-$C3); a voice whose entry is $FF is left as it is. The processor's interrupt flag is kept
builds the music's frequency table at $C000: eight octaves of twelve notes, 192 bytes, each octave the top one ($2894) shifted right, note n at $C000 + 2n; then silences the SID ($2482)
silences the music: clears the SID's registers ($D401 on) and the driver's variables ($A0-$DF), and sets the pulse sweep's start to $0400

plays one frame of music, from the raster interrupt. For each voice, 3 down to 1: when the note's frames run out the gate is let go, unless held, and the next commands and note are read ($24BD); then the pulse width sweep for the voices that have it ($CC), up and down between $0200 and $0E00 by $0F a frame, or $10 when the carry is left set (nothing clears it before the addition), and the vibrato for those that have it ($D2), each voice's frequency moved up or down by its step and turned round after its period
reads the voice's next byte: $EA is skipped, $FF ends the voice (pointer cleared, gate off), below $C0 a note ($27E4), otherwise a command from the table at $2852
the pulse width, the same for every voice that sweeps

the vibrato: every voice in $D2 counts its period down ($D9) and turns its direction round (bit 7 of $D4) when it runs out, adding or subtracting the step to its frequency; then the three frequencies are written to the SID
the offset of each voice's registers from $D400: 0, 7 and 14
command $C1: the voice's frequency, two bytes, straight to the SID
command $DD: a pulse wave ($40) with the pulse width at $0800
command $C2: the voice's waveform (its control register without the gate), one byte
command $C3: the voice's pulse width, two bytes
command $C4: the voice's envelope, attack-decay then sustain-release
command $C5: the filter's cutoff, low then high byte
command $C9: lowers the filter's cutoff by a byte, then reads a length as a note does
command $D6: raises the filter's cutoff by a byte, then a length
command $C6: the filter's resonance, the high nibble of a byte
command $C0: adds a byte to the volume, the result kept below 16
command $C7: the volume, the low nibble of a byte, with the filter type kept
command $C8: a wait: the voice reads nothing more for that many frames
command $CA: puts the voice through the filter
command $CB: the filter type, the high nibble of a byte, with the volume kept
command $CC: takes the voice out of the filter
command $CD: sets the voice's first repeat count ($B7)
command $CE: a repeat: two bytes, an address the voice goes back to until the first repeat count runs out
command $D1: sets the voice's second repeat count ($B4)
command $D2: the second repeat, as $CE with the count at $B4
command $DA: lowers the frequency's high byte by a byte, then a length
command $CF: lowers the frequency by a byte, then a length
command $D9: raises the frequency's high byte by a byte, then a length
command $D0: raises the frequency by a byte, then a length
command $DB: vibrato on for the voice: its step and direction ($D4), then its period ($D3, $D9)
command $DC: vibrato off for the voice
command $D3: pulse width sweep on for the voice
command $D4: pulse width sweep off for the voice
each voice's bit, 1, 2 and 4, for the driver's masks of voices
command $D7: detune on for the voice: a byte the note's frequency is lowered by
command $D5: a random note, number 31 to 95, which the SID's voice 3 output ($D41B) picks

command $DE: sets $DC to $FF, lets the gate go, and ends the voice's reading for the frame. The waveform it reads is at $AE plus twice the voice's number, X still holding the data pointer's index: the right one for voice 1 only
command $DF: sets the voice's bit in $DD and stores a byte in $DE
command $E0: clears the voice's bit in $DD

a note: two times its number indexes the frequency table at $C000; the rest note, $60, only lets the gate go. The frequency goes to the SID, lowered by the voice's detune if it has it; the gate on. Then its length ($282C)
the note's length: bit 7 holds the gate when the length runs out, bits 0-6 are the frames
the next byte of the voice's data, through its pointer at $A0 + $BF, which steps on
where each command, $C0 to $E0, is handled
the twelve notes of the top octave, C to B, as SID frequencies ($861E to $FD2E); $244A shifts them for the seven octaves below
where each octave starts in the frequency table at $C000, by the number of shifts plus one: the first byte is not read

each tune's tracks, four bytes a tune from tune 1, voices 1 to 3 and a fourth byte not read; $FF leaves a voice alone. The event plays 1 at the start, 2 after a good toss, 3, 4 and 7 at moments of the throw, 5 and 6 with the run's poses, 8 in a caber move; tune 9 is never played
where each of the 22 tracks is
the tracks: notes, lengths and commands, each to $FF, to $2E3A
sprite shapes, 64 bytes each, the 64th the colour and flags
sprite shapes $4C00 to $4FFF, for poses $04 to $07 and $0C to $11
sprite shapes $5000 to $53FF, for poses $11, $13 to $2E, $30, $31, $38 to $40 and $47 to $4A
sprite shapes $5400 to $57FF, for poses $17 to $1B, $1D to $20, $25, $27 to $2B, $2D to $2F, $3B to $3E, $47 and $49
sprite shapes $5800 to $5BFF, for poses $1B, $1F, $20, $23 to $25, $28 to $2B, $2F, $3B, $3D, $3F, $47, $4C and $4D
sprite shapes $5C00 to $5FFF, for poses $2C and $2E to $33
sprite shapes $6100 to $663F, for poses $35 to $3A
sprite shapes $6500 to $663F, for poses $39 and $3A, the lift
sprite shapes for poses $3B on; after a good toss, or once the caber has fallen back, they and the second set at $A000 change places a page a frame ($1EB2), and change back for the next attempt
sprite shapes $6A40 to $6E3F, for poses $42 to $4A and $5B to $5F (the set the swap changes)
sprite shapes $6E40 to $723F, for poses $4B to $53, $5F to $66 and $73 to $76 (the set the swap changes)
sprite shapes $7240 to $763F, for poses $4F to $56 and $66 to $76 (the set the swap changes)
sprite shapes $7640 to $77FF, for poses $6B, $71, $74 and $75 (the set the swap changes)
the character set's second half, characters $80 to $FF
the top six rows of the screen
row 4 of the top rows, as the screen shows it
row 5 of the top rows, the last
128 bytes the code here does not read, to $816F

the second set of sprite shapes, 18 pages to $B1BF, swapped in for the toss
the second set's last pages, to $B1BF
bytes nothing reads, to $B3FF, in the pattern of $00 and $FF that memory holds at power-on
